title: Hiring a broker does not transfer every franchise-sales duty
seoTitle: Franchise brokers: claims and FDD responsibilities
description: Know what remains your responsibility when someone else recruits franchisees.
learningSummary: Your broker’s statements can matter under the federal Franchise Rule. The franchisor remains responsible for furnishing the Franchise Disclosure Document, or FDD.

sections.heading: The broker and franchisor have different duties
paragraphs: The federal definition of franchise seller can include employees, agents, subfranchisors and outside brokers involved in sales. Seller-conduct restrictions reach those people; responsibility for furnishing the FDD rests with the franchisor. A referral contract saying the broker handles compliance does not transfer every duty.
This includes substantive claims in an introduction. What the speaker actually says matters more than calling the candidate an investor or describing the contact as a referral.

sections.heading: A broker’s private spreadsheet can create the same problem as your deck
paragraphs: In a fictional cleaning offer, a broker says a hired local manager can produce a predictable margin. That is a statement about the proposed business’s financial result, not simply an exchange of contact details. Check its Item 19 treatment and written support before it is repeated. Item 19 is the FDD section addressing financial performance representations.

Sellers must not contradict required disclosures or misrepresent a reference as independent. Performance claims need the applicable reasonable basis, written supporting evidence and disclosure treatment, whether made in a webinar, portal, spreadsheet or private conversation.

sections.heading: Control the message and the formal delivery
paragraphs: Give the broker materials that match the actual disclosure, make clear who may answer financial-result questions and retain the communications actually used. Separately, make sure the correct FDD is furnished to the prospect under the applicable timetable. One task does not demonstrate that the other happened.

practicalOutput: Check the broker’s actual sales message and confirm who will furnish the current FDD before recruitment proceeds.
limitations: This is the federal distinction. State broker licensing, registration, advertising and authority to sell require separate checks; the fictional example establishes no violation.
editNote: Removed the repetitive responsibility table, glossary and sheet instructions; retained two duties and one broker-message example.
conditionsRetained: Broad seller definition and franchisor FDD-furnishing responsibility preserved.
Seller claims cannot contradict disclosures or misrepresent independent references; FPR basis/support/treatment retained.
Private/broker channels and actual statements covered; no automatic fictional violation.
Independent state broker/sales rules retained.

title: Can you advertise a target margin to U.S. franchise buyers?
seoTitle: Franchise advertising: when a target margin needs support
description: Changing an achieved home-market result into a target does not explain its basis for a U.S. buyer.
learningSummary: An accurate number can create an unsupported impression. Read the whole advertisement as a prospective franchisee would, including its images, caption and surrounding explanation.

sections.heading: What target 20% leaves unanswered
paragraphs: A fictional technical-services brand has one home-country unit with a 20% operating margin. Its U.S. deck says target 20%. The new word does not show why a U.S. operator could achieve that result, what costs were included or how representative that unit was.

Not every brand message is a financial performance representation. Where the message is one, the applicable reasonable basis, written support and disclosure requirements must be satisfied. Compare the actual statement with Item 19, the FDD’s financial-performance section. A disclaimer does not cure a contradiction with required disclosure.

sections.heading: Keep the meaning attached to the figure
paragraphs: Revenue and profit are different. The period, geography, included and excluded units, operating model and omitted costs can change what a figure tells the buyer. A successful home-market outlet does not alone justify a U.S. performance claim.
Testimonials need attention too, including incentives given to references and any claim that a reference is independent. Save the advertisement in the form actually used—not just an isolated number.

sections.heading: Correct every live version
paragraphs: If the underlying information changes, find the slides, landing pages, scripts and broker material using it. Updating your master deck leaves the old message in circulation if a broker still uses a previous copy.

practicalOutput: Decide whether the proposed message has the necessary support and disclosure treatment before publishing it; withdraw superseded copies.
limitations: No advertisement is approved here. State advertising filings, required wording, broker rules and sales authority remain separate.
editNote: Cut the duplicate table and claim-register instructions; kept the target-margin misconception and the costs/sample context it omits.
conditionsRetained: Not every brand message is an FPR; actual audience/context controls.
Reasonable basis/written support/disclosure and no contradiction retained.
20% is fictional home-unit margin, not an approved U.S. forecast.
Testimonials/reference independence and live-version updates retained.
Separate state advertising requirements retained.

title: Customer promises and the federal Business Opportunity Rule
seoTitle: Business Opportunity Rule: promised accounts versus advice
description: A promise of customers, locations or buyback can raise a separate federal disclosure question.
learningSummary: A marketing course and a promise of named customer accounts are different offers. Under Part 437, assess the purchaser’s new business, required payment and the specified promise together.

sections.heading: What the purchaser is buying
paragraphs: The new-business question concerns the purchaser, not how long your brand has operated. The definition also requires payment and specified representations that you or a designated person will provide locations, customers or accounts, or buy back what the purchaser produces.

The customer-provision definition can reach recommended lead-generation or locator services, customer lists and some payment-collection arrangements. General business-development advice, training and advertising alone are not treated as providing customers under that definition.

sections.heading: An established buyer can still be entering a new line
paragraphs: In a fictional offer, an existing facilities operator buys a new cleaning line, required software and a promise of named accounts. Existing trading does not itself answer whether this is a new business or line for that purchaser. Nor does calling the promise marketing support explain whether the seller will teach marketing or provide customers.

sections.heading: The duties and the unresolved exemption issue
paragraphs: Where Part 437 applies, give its prescribed written disclosure and applicable earnings information at least seven calendar days before the earlier binding agreement or payment/other consideration. Retain the specified disclosure versions, receipts, contracts and earnings support for three years.

The exemption interaction remains unresolved. Section 437.8 literally uses less than $500 while referring to section 436.8(a)(1); that section currently uses less than $735. Reading both provisions does not settle how the cross-reference applies. Do not use either amount alone to declare the offer exempt.

practicalOutput: Describe the exact customer, location or buyback promise before taking money; do not assume an exemption from the unresolved cross-reference.
limitations: Franchise coverage and independent state business-opportunity/franchise duties still require their own assessment.
editNote: Removed the duplicated scope table and internal research instructions; narrowed the page to the promise distinction and stated the exemption hold once. Source follow-up: Actual current Part 437 and section 436.8 confirm the literal $500/$735 discrepancy. No reviewed primary interpretation settles the $500–$734.99 interaction or makes the cross-reference self-correcting.
conditionsRetained: Purchaser-new-business, payment and specified seller/designated-person representations all retained.
General advice/training/advertising alone versus specified customer provision retained.
Seven CALENDAR days before earlier agreement/payment/other consideration; three-year specified records.
Literal Part437 $500/current Part436 cross-reference hold retained without resolving it.
Independent franchise/state layers retained.
Source follow-up scope: Authoritative interpretation of section 437.8(a), not access to its literal wording.

title: Does your U.S. company need to register in another state?
seoTitle: U.S. formation versus foreign qualification in another state
description: Creating the company and obtaining authority for its activities elsewhere are different decisions.
learningSummary: A company has a legal home where it is formed. Another state may require that same company to register for its activities there—a process commonly called foreign qualification.

sections.heading: Foreign can mean another U.S. state
paragraphs: For this purpose, a Delaware company can be foreign in Texas even if every owner is American. The term is about the company’s formation jurisdiction, not the owner’s nationality.

The Small Business Administration describes possible certificates of authority and, in many states, good-standing evidence. Its overview does not establish one nationwide activity threshold, exception or fee. Those come from the relevant state requirements.

sections.heading: A Delaware record does not settle a Texas depot
paragraphs: In a fictional plan, a Singapore-owned business forms a Delaware LLC and proposes a staffed Texas service depot. Formation proves the entity was created in Delaware. It does not determine Texas qualification, payroll accounts, customer-site licences or the depot’s occupancy conditions.

The qualification question concerns what this entity will do: who employs the staff, holds premises, signs customer contracts and performs the work. A website, one customer or an owner’s address is not a universal answer. This example makes no finding that a particular Texas filing is required.

sections.heading: Registration is not the whole launch
paragraphs: Keep company qualification separate from tax accounts, franchise sales, sector licences and premises permissions. Where registration brings registered-agent or annual-report responsibilities, those also need to be maintained. It is not automatically a reason to form another subsidiary.

practicalOutput: Check the actual activities of your existing entity against the state’s qualification requirements before treating its formation certificate as operating authority.
limitations: This SBA-based explanation determines no state threshold, exemption, fee or tax connection.
editNote: Removed the duplicate depot table and entity register; kept the meaning of foreign and what the formation certificate does not establish.
conditionsRetained: Foreign means formed elsewhere, including another U.S.state, not foreign ownership.
State-specific actual activity/exceptions; no universal customer/website test.
Original Delaware/Texas/Singapore depot example retained without filing finding.
Qualification, taxes, operating permissions and recurring responsibilities remain distinct.

title: What federal tax treatment does your LLC have?
seoTitle: LLC default tax treatment and Form 8832 elections
description: Legal form, default tax classification and an election are separate matters.
learningSummary: The name LLC does not choose its federal tax treatment. Start with the entity’s eligibility, place of formation and owners, then any valid election.

sections.heading: The domestic defaults
paragraphs: For a domestic eligible entity, two or more members generally mean partnership treatment by default; one owner generally means disregarded treatment unless an election applies. Disregarded is a tax classification, not a statement that the company has no legal existence or reporting work.
Foreign-entity defaults differ and depend partly on limited liability. Do not apply the domestic subsidiary’s default to the overseas parent.

sections.heading: An election has an effective date as well as a filing date
paragraphs: An eligible entity uses the defined election procedure, including Form 8832. The ordinary effective date can be up to 75 days before filing or up to 12 months after filing. A change election generally faces a 60-month restriction, subject to exceptions; an initial election effective on formation is treated differently.

Late relief has conditions. A desired effective date does not become valid merely because it is written on the form. The retrieved form’s December 2013 revision date is not a different election deadline.

sections.heading: One owner does not mean no information return
paragraphs: In a fictional example, an overseas company forms a one-member domestic LLC and assumes disregarded treatment means no U.S. information return. Foreign-owner funding and related transactions can raise separate Form 5472 and accompanying pro forma return questions. Classification and information reporting must each be addressed.

practicalOutput: Establish the actual default and any election’s validity and dates before using that treatment in a return.
limitations: This does not select an entity or election, establish late relief, or decide state tax, treaty, reporting or immigration outcomes.
editNote: Cut repeated election-table and brief instructions; placed defaults, election limits and the separate reporting consequence in three short sections.
conditionsRetained: Eligible/domestic one-owner and two-plus-owner defaults retained; foreign defaults/limited liability distinction.
Ordinary 75 days BEFORE and 12 months AFTER filing; general 60-month change restriction; initial-formation/exception treatment.
Conditional late relief; existing form revision not advanced.
Disregarded classification does not remove foreign-owner information reporting; no chosen outcome.

title: Why your usual royalty is not a transfer-pricing answer
seoTitle: Parent royalties: the starting transfer-pricing questions
description: A standard group percentage does not establish an arm’s-length charge to the U.S. subsidiary.
learningSummary: Related-company charges need a basis in the actual transaction. Saying our royalty is 6% states a policy; it does not show why that price fits the rights and services being supplied.

sections.heading: One invoice can contain several activities
paragraphs: A parent may license a name, train staff, provide ongoing technical support, lend capital and supply products. Identify what each company actually does, what it supplies and who benefits. One invoice does not make the underlying activities identical.

In a fictional case, a single royalty covers the brand, initial training and quarterly support. The subsidiary also performs its own sales and support work. Those facts matter before copying a rate paid by an unrelated franchisee with different rights and services.

sections.heading: What the general rule requires
paragraphs: The arm’s-length standard compares results with dealings between unrelated taxpayers in comparable circumstances. Under the best-method rule, the most reliable measure depends on comparability, data quality and assumptions—not a universal preferred percentage.

For intellectual property, identify who develops, owns, funds and maintains it. For services, identify the work, staff time, costs and beneficiaries. Functions, assets and risks mean what each company does, uses and bears. This does not mean every activity must be separately priced or every cost is chargeable.

sections.heading: Price and withholding are different questions
paragraphs: Transfer pricing concerns the controlled price. Withholding concerns what tax the payer deducts from the payment. A supported price does not itself settle treaty relief or the foreign country’s rules.

practicalOutput: Explain what the U.S. company receives and what both companies actually do before fixing the intercompany rate.
limitations: This covers the general standard in §1.482-1(a)–(c), not a selected method, royalty rate, valuation, complete documentation rule or penalty defence.
editNote: Scoped the promise to the general standard and removed the repeated invoice table and pricing-file inventory.
conditionsRetained: Arm’s-length/best-method standards; comparability/data/assumptions retained.
6% remains an unsupported policy illustration; no rate/method selected.
Actual functions/assets/risks and bundled services retained without requiring separate prices or chargeable costs.
General a–c scope; documentation/penalty/foreign-law/treaty/withholding limits retained.

title: Meetings and repair work are different U.S. trip activities
seoTitle: U.S. business visits: negotiations versus hands-on work
description: A business purpose does not make every task on the trip permissible visitor activity.
learningSummary: The important question is what you will do in America. Negotiating a contract and performing a customer’s ordinary work are different activities, even on the same trip.

sections.heading: What the general visitor examples establish
paragraphs: The State Department lists consulting business associates, attending relevant conferences and negotiating contracts as business-visitor examples. It lists employment as not permitted on visitor visas.
Owning the U.S. company or being paid overseas does not alone decide whether your planned task is permitted. These examples are not an individual visa or admission decision.

sections.heading: A meeting followed by two weeks of repairs
paragraphs: A fictional technical founder plans three days negotiating a distribution contract, then two weeks repairing customer equipment beside the U.S. team. The negotiation example does not establish permission for the repairs.

Before promising that presence to a customer, separate the duties, who benefits, location, duration, payment and repeat-visit pattern. Training, installation, hands-on service and ordinary management cannot all be treated as meetings under a heading such as launch support.

sections.heading: Permission for the person still matters
paragraphs: A visa does not guarantee admission; the admitting authorities decide entry. If the operational work requires a different staffing arrangement, that affects the launch plan. An L-1, E-2 or another work-authorised route is a separate question, not an alternative assumed to be available.

practicalOutput: Resolve the actual operating work on the trip before bookings or customer commitments depend on you performing it.
limitations: This gives no individual visa, ESTA, admission, productive-training, installation or hands-on-service conclusion.
editNote: Removed the duplicate itinerary table, activity-brief glossary and handoff language; retained the mixed-trip problem.
conditionsRetained: Permitted general examples versus employment exclusion; no individual ruling.
Original three-day negotiation/two-week repair example retained.
Ownership/foreign pay alone insufficient; actual activity/location/duration/payment/repeat pattern retained.
Visa not guaranteed admission; no assumed alternative category.

title: A quiet week does not cancel last week’s overtime
seoTitle: Federal overtime: a 45-hour workweek calculation
description: Budget covered nonexempt work by the fixed workweek, not a two-week average.
learningSummary: For a covered nonexempt employee, the federal baseline is generally at least one-and-one-half the regular rate for hours over 40 in a fixed workweek. Salary and a manager title do not by themselves establish an exemption.

sections.heading: A small launch can still be covered
paragraphs: Department of Labor guidance distinguishes enterprise coverage from individual coverage. The ordinary enterprise test includes at least two employees and at least $500,000 in annual business volume; specified institutions receive different treatment. Individual interstate-commerce coverage can apply even below that volume.

A modest startup budget therefore does not settle coverage. Nor does an advance-approval policy waive overtime already earned. Exemption depends on the actual duties, compensation and applicable rules.

sections.heading: Fictional example: 45 hours at a $20 regular rate
paragraphs: Assume the employee is covered and nonexempt, and no other compensation affects the $20 regular rate. This illustration excludes employer costs.

rows: Extra half-time premium on the five overtime hours

sections.heading: Why 35 hours next week does not change it
paragraphs: The workweek is a fixed 168-hour period. A following 35-hour week does not erase the five overtime hours by producing a two-week average of 40.

The extra premium above is half-time because straight time was already counted for all 45 hours. Other compensation, including bonuses, can change the regular-rate calculation. State or local wage rules and leave, payroll taxes and other employer costs also affect the actual staffing budget.

practicalOutput: Price expected busy workweeks using the applicable pay rules rather than averaging them against quieter weeks.
limitations: This supplies no current salary-exemption threshold or contractor/joint-employer determination, and no complete regular-rate or state/local calculation.
editNote: Kept the useful overtime arithmetic once, removed duplicate prose calculation and staffing-record instructions.
conditionsRetained: Enterprise ordinary two employees/$500,000; institution exception and separate individual coverage retained.
Covered nonexempt over40 fixed168hour workweek; no averaging; salary/title not exemption; earned overtime not waived.
Original45/35/$20/$900/$50/$950 plus equivalent40×20+5×30 retained once with no-other-compensation assumption.
Regular rate/bonuses/state/local and employer-cost limits retained.

title: Who remains responsible for safety at a customer site?
seoTitle: Employer safety duties at customer premises
description: A customer induction or a brand manual does not establish that the employer has met its safety duties.
learningSummary: Working at someone else’s premises does not make safety only the customer’s problem. The actual employer, task and control of the work matter.

sections.heading: The employer duty is more than a contract clause
paragraphs: OSH Act section 5(a) requires a covered employer to provide a workplace free of recognised hazards causing or likely to cause death or serious physical harm, and to comply with applicable occupational safety and health standards.

A clause saying the local operator handles safety does not demonstrate that equipment, training and hazards have been addressed. Equally, the brand being overseas does not by itself decide its legal responsibility.

sections.heading: Law, customer rules and brand standards are different
paragraphs: A customer’s induction, insurance certificate and site rules can be part of the job arrangements. They do not establish compliance with every applicable standard. Identify the actual chemicals, equipment, access conditions and task hazards, and the federal OSHA or state-plan authority involved.

In a fictional case, a brand gives remote training before its partner’s employees service powered machinery at a customer site. If the general-industry hazardous-energy standard applies, the employer needs the required energy-control programme, procedures, training and inspections; a customer induction alone does not do that. Its scope and exceptions matter: for example, its cord-and-plug exception requires unplugging to control the hazard and the plug to remain under the servicing employee’s exclusive control.

practicalOutput: Establish the actual job’s equipment, training and safety requirements before relying on a customer induction or general brand course.
limitations: This is an employer-duty baseline, not a task-specific OSHA or state-plan controls guide. It supplies no incident deadline or joint-employer determination.
editNote: Narrowed to the employer-duty distinction; removed the empty job card and repeated readiness-file disclaimers. Source follow-up: Read section5 employer duties and the actual 1910.147 scope/programme text. The proposed replacement teaches one conditional machinery-servicing control rather than implying that an induction satisfies law or prescribing lockout for all powered equipment. Source follow-up: Read section5 employer duties and the actual 1910.147 scope/programme text. The proposed replacement teaches one conditional machinery-servicing control rather than implying that an induction satisfies law or prescribing lockout for all powered equipment.
conditionsRetained: Covered-employer recognised-serious-hazard and applicable-standard duties retained.
Actual control/employment facts; foreign location/contract clause/induction not decisive.
Original remote-powered-equipment example retained without training-compliance finding.
Task/state-plan/incident/joint-employer scope remains unprovided, not implicitly cleared.
Source follow-up scope: Job-specific applicability, other standards and state-plan requirements remain outside this baseline.

title: Form I-9: completion and retention deadlines
seoTitle: Form I-9 completion deadlines and retention dates
description: Know the employee and employer deadlines, including the shorter-employment exception and the later retention date.
learningSummary: The hiring employer needs an I-9 process even if its owner stays overseas. This page explains federal completion and retention deadlines; the current USCIS form edition and detailed examination instructions were not verified in the recorded review.

sections.heading: Employee and employer steps have different deadlines
paragraphs: Form I-9 records employment eligibility verification. Under the cited regulation, the employee completes Section 1 at hire. The employer generally examines the required acceptable evidence and completes Section 2 within three business days of hire.

If employment lasts less than three business days, the employer’s examination and completion take place at hire instead, and a receipt cannot replace the required document. The regulation permits the employer, its agent or someone acting in its interest to perform the employer step. Arrange who will do it before work starts; ownership overseas does not change the deadlines or authorise an informal remote check.

sections.heading: A deadline does not establish a permitted checking method
paragraphs: The regulation recognises physical examination or an alternative procedure authorised under its specified conditions. A video call, emailed scan or overseas manager’s review is not automatically an authorised method. Use the official instructions to establish the applicable examination process before relying on it.

sections.heading: Keep the later of two retention dates
paragraphs: Retain the I-9 for three years after hire or one year after termination, whichever is later.

In a fictional example, an employee starts on January 15, 2027 and leaves on January 15, 2030. Three years after hire is January 15, 2030; one year after departure is January 15, 2031. The later date, January 15, 2031, controls this I-9 calculation. Other record-retention duties are separate.

practicalOutput: Arrange a compliant examination process before the hire, and calculate both retention dates when employment ends.
limitations: This page does not determine individual work authorisation, E-Verify, anti-discrimination or visa-category questions.
editNote: Scoped the headline to the verified deadlines; removed repeated hiring table, task-register and site-storage prose. The unresolved form/procedure issue appears once in the introduction. Source follow-up: The current regulation verifies the deadlines, the short-employment no-receipt condition, agent language and later-of-two-dates retention. The complete 2023 DHS notice verifies a specifically conditioned alternative procedure. USCIS current form/instructions and E-Verify update pages remain403. Reginfo lists an active2024 approval and a pending2026 extension; pending attached instruments are not treated as authorised current editions.

Employment lasting LESS THAN three business days: examination/completion at hire.
Physical or specifically authorised alternative examination; no informal remote approval.
Current USCIS form/procedure source hold remains explicit.

title: A customs broker does not settle who imports your goods
seoTitle: Importer of record versus customs broker responsibilities
description: Choose the actual importing arrangement before sending equipment to a partner’s warehouse.
learningSummary: The warehouse address tells you where the equipment will arrive. It does not establish the importer of record or the broker’s authority to make entry.

sections.heading: Who carries the entry responsibility?
paragraphs: The importer of record must use reasonable care in supplying the relevant customs entry and completion information. The eligible-filer rules include an owner or purchaser and an appropriately designated licensed person under the stated conditions.

Identify the actual seller, owner, purchaser, consignee, broker and recipient. One company may have several roles. A forwarder’s name on a quote does not establish those roles or remove the need for accurate information.

sections.heading: Demonstration machines still need an importing arrangement
paragraphs: In a fictional shipment, an overseas brand sends demonstration machines to a partner’s U.S. warehouse and assumes the warehouse will handle importation. Before dispatch, establish who will make entry, their authority, the machines’ value and use, and whether they will return or stay.

The party making entry needs evidence of its right to do so through the specified shipping-document arrangements. The commercial invoice and product description must support the classification, value and origin information. Product-agency requirements are separate.

sections.heading: Do not use one deletion date for every customs document
paragraphs: The general customs retention period is five years from entry or the activity creating the record. There are category-specific exceptions, including particular drawback, packing-list, informal-consignee and carrier records. Identify the record category before applying a deletion date.

practicalOutput: Confirm who has the entry role and authority, and provide the shipment facts before the goods leave.
limitations: This does not decide product classification, value, bond requirements, nonresident-importer eligibility or agency admissibility. Retention exceptions remain category-specific.
editNote: Removed the repetitive shipment-role table and document-sheet instructions; kept responsibility, authority and the actual demonstration-shipment problem.
conditionsRetained: Eligible filer/designated licensed person conditions and reasonable care retained.
Evidence of right to enter and actual shipment information retained.
Demonstration use/return questions not decided; no importer role assigned by warehouse address.
Five-year general clock with named category exceptions retained; product/nonresident/bond/value unresolved.

title: Why an equipment label is not enough for a duty quote
seoTitle: Product facts needed for a U.S. import-duty estimate
description: A scrubber and a replacement battery may need different tariff answers, even on one shipment.
learningSummary: A budget line saying cleaning equipment at 5% is an assumption, not a product-specific tariff answer. The goods and current provisions must support the rate.

sections.heading: Start with what is actually entering
paragraphs: A tariff classification identifies goods under the U.S. Harmonized Tariff Schedule, or HTS. Record each product’s function, materials, composition, dimensions and how it is presented at entry. Customs entry completion requires classification and rate information.

In a fictional example, a brand combines a powered floor scrubber and replacement battery under cleaning equipment at 5%. The catalogue category does not establish that they share a classification or rate. The 5% is invented and is not a rate asserted for either item.

sections.heading: Separate the duty questions
paragraphs: The base tariff can differ from additional measures, exclusions or a claimed preference. Chapter 99 contains provisions that may add or modify treatment. The relevant date, product, origin and provision matter; an unexplained combined percentage hides those questions.

Landed cost is the cost of getting the goods to their destination, not just the purchase price or base duty. An unverified rate can be a labelled sensitivity assumption, but cannot be treated as a confirmed cost.

sections.heading: A calculator is not a binding classification ruling
paragraphs: USITC’s official HTS help points to classification rules, legal notes, schedule provisions and Customs and Border Protection ruling resources. A commercial calculator does not itself supply a binding ruling. Revisit the estimate when the product, supplier, production origin or applicable provisions change.

practicalOutput: Obtain a supported answer for each actual product before using an assumed percentage as the launch budget’s duty figure.
limitations: No code, current rate, Chapter 99 treatment, exclusion, preference or trade-remedy result is verified here. Origin marking and product admissibility are separate.
editNote: Scoped the headline to missing product facts; removed the unverified-rate table, quiz and rate-ledger ceremony.
conditionsRetained: Original scrubber/battery and fictional5% retained without actual classification/rate.
Materials/function/composition/dimensions/entry presentation; HTS notes/rulings scope retained.
Base versus additional/Chapter99/preference/date/origin distinctions retained.
No current rate/code/exclusion verified; nonbinding calculator and separate marking/admissibility retained.

title: What can your equipment’s origin label actually say?
seoTitle: Country-of-origin marking versus brand nationality
description: The brand’s home country, component origin, assembly location and departure port are different facts.
learningSummary: A European brand sticker identifies the brand, not necessarily the equipment’s country of origin. Work through how the product is made before treating the label as established.

sections.heading: Manufacturing steps matter
paragraphs: The marking framework starts with manufacture, production or growth and considers whether further work effects substantial transformation. The rule directs relevant NAFTA/USMCA-country marking cases to the special Part 102 provisions; one general transformation approach cannot be assumed for every product.

In a fictional case, components are made in one country and assembled in another. The words assembled in another country do not themselves establish that origin changed. What happened to the materials and product before and after the work matters.

sections.heading: What the general marking rule requires
paragraphs: Foreign-origin articles, or their containers as applicable, generally must show the English country name conspicuously, legibly, indelibly and with sufficient permanence for the ultimate U.S. purchaser. A country mentioned only in paperwork does not necessarily meet those qualities.
Exceptions and special rules can change the answer for particular articles, containers or subsequent operations. This guide determines neither the fictional product’s origin nor a marking exception.

sections.heading: Marking is not a tariff-preference decision
paragraphs: Brand ownership, departure port, marking origin and preferential tariff origin are distinct. A conclusion for a label does not automatically establish tariff preference or trade-remedy treatment. A supplier or manufacturing-process change can also make an old label conclusion unsuitable for the new goods.

practicalOutput: Check the actual production steps and proposed label together before printing it for the U.S. shipment.
limitations: No product-specific substantial-transformation, Part 102, marking-exception, preference or trade-remedy finding is made here; other product labels need their own review.
editNote: Removed the duplicate supply-chain table and manufacturing-map handoff; focused on the proposed label and production facts.
conditionsRetained: Manufacture/production/growth, substantial transformation and relevant Part102 special cases retained.
English country-name marking qualities/ultimate purchaser/container qualification/exceptions retained.
Original multi-country example makes no origin finding.
Brand/shipping/marking/preference distinctions and process-change implications retained.

title: Who is the FSVP importer for your food shipment?
seoTitle: FSVP importer versus customs broker for food shipments
description: Food-supplier verification has its own importer definition; the freight booking does not decide it.
learningSummary: Under the Foreign Supplier Verification Programs rules, the responsible importer can be different from the customs importer or broker. Establish that role before treating a supplier certificate as the food-import answer.

sections.heading: Start with the owner or consignee at entry
paragraphs: The FSVP importer is the defined U.S. owner or consignee of the food offered for import. If none exists at entry, the role falls to the specified U.S. agent or representative of the foreign owner or consignee, with the required signed consent.
A freight forwarder or foreign-facility registration contact is not automatically that importer. Identify which actual party satisfies the definition.

sections.heading: Verification depends on the food and supplier
paragraphs: An importer within scope generally must develop, maintain and follow a programme for each imported food, subject to the applicable exceptions. FDA’s overview covers qualified individuals, hazard analysis, supplier evaluation, appropriate verification, corrective action and reevaluation.

A fictional brand sends packaged snacks to a U.S. partner for resale. Its food, producer, U.S. purchaser at entry and available verification evidence must be identified. Neither small quantity nor company size alone establishes an exemption or modified treatment. One certificate is not automatically the programme, but neither does every case require the same audit or a separate physical document for each food/supplier combination.

sections.heading: The programme does not replace entry information
paragraphs: Each line entry needs the required importer name, email and FDA-acceptable unique facility identifier, and designation where relevant before import. Labelling, prior notice, facility registration and other admissibility duties remain separate.
Specified USDA-regulated meat, poultry and egg products fall outside FSVP under the stated exemptions. That does not make them unrestricted imports.

practicalOutput: Identify the defined FSVP importer and the food/supplier verification responsibility before dispatching the snacks or other food.
limitations: This does not determine a food category, hazard, small-importer or supplement exception, complete USDA treatment or shipment admissibility.

title: Is an exact U.S. trademark search enough?
seoTitle: Exact trademark searches versus broader U.S. clearance
description: A clean exact-name result can miss similar marks and related uses.
learningSummary: Before committing to signs or software branding, search the actual U.S. offer—not just the spelling and service category you used at home.

sections.heading: The search is wider than identical names
paragraphs: USPTO recommends a comprehensive search for confusingly similar marks for the same or related goods and services. Sound, spelling, appearance and meaning can matter. Federal registered and pending records are important, but relevant state records and common-law marketplace use can also matter.

Include the word mark, logo, abbreviations, translations and intended goods or services. A differently spelled name is not automatically irrelevant, and an empty exact-name list is not legal clearance.

sections.heading: The facilities business also sells an app
paragraphs: A fictional facilities group finds no exact federal match in cleaning services. It plans to license both its name and a scheduling app, and initially treats the result as permission to order signs.

The search omitted part of the actual offer. Similar marks and related software/service uses also need examination. The example does not establish a conflict or registrability; it explains why that first result is too narrow to support the spending decision.

sections.heading: A result still needs interpretation
paragraphs: Distinguish registered or pending status from observed use, and record uncertain first-use or geographic facts accurately. A match does not alone decide confusion either. Registration strategy, ownership permissions and licence quality controls are separate from searching for competing rights.

practicalOutput: Include the complete U.S. offer and relevant similar uses before relying on an exact-name search to launch the brand.
limitations: This gives no clearance opinion, confusion finding, registration guarantee or complete ownership/licence assessment.
editNote: Cut the empty results table and repeated clearance-brief instructions; retained the missing app category as the practical lesson.
conditionsRetained: Comprehensive similarity factors/related goodsservices and federal/state/commonlaw scope retained.
Actual marks/logos/abbreviations/translations and result-status uncertainties retained.

title: Sharing know-how takes more than a confidential label
seoTitle: Trade-secret access controls and protected disclosures
description: Give people the information needed for their work while preserving the law’s protected-reporting rules.
learningSummary: A manager may need manuals and technical methods, but not every company file. Trade-secret protection depends on the information’s secrecy and value, not simply the heading on an agreement.

sections.heading: What makes information a trade secret
paragraphs: The federal definition requires reasonable secrecy measures and independent economic value from not being generally known or readily ascertainable by proper means. Public marketing material does not become secret because the contract says confidential. Lawful independent development and reverse engineering are not automatically misappropriation.

In a fictional training business, a manager receives every manual, customer record and pricing file. Separate public material, genuinely claimed secrets and personal data. Limit access to what the role needs and plan how accounts and retained copies are handled on exit. These are business measures relevant to secrecy, not proof that every file is legally protected.

sections.heading: Confidentiality cannot erase the specified reporting protection
paragraphs: The law protects specified confidential disclosures to government officials or an attorney solely to report or investigate suspected legal violations, and sealed court filings under its conditions. Covered employer agreements about secrets or confidential information need the immunity notice or a qualifying policy reference.

For this provision, employee includes individual contractors and consultants. The notice rule applies to agreements entered into or updated after May 11, 2016. Missing it limits the specified exemplary-damages and attorney-fee remedies against the affected employee; it does not automatically void the agreement or remove every remedy. Not every company-to-company franchise agreement is covered.

practicalOutput: Decide which actual information each recipient needs, how access ends and whether the recipient’s agreement falls within the notice rule.
limitations: No file is declared a trade secret here. State law, remedies and personal-data/cross-border privacy obligations remain separate.
editNote: Removed duplicated materials table and remedy paragraph; focused on access decisions and one complete explanation of the notice rule.
conditionsRetained: Reasonable secrecy measures plus independent secrecy-based economic value retained.
Proper means/independent development/reverse engineering distinction retained.
Protected disclosure purposes/recipients/sealed conditions and qualifying notice/policy route retained.
Individual contractors/consultants; agreements entered or updated after2016-05-11; precise limited remedy effect not voidall retained.
Company-company scope and separate personal-data/state law retained.

title: Can your technical leader fill the planned L-1 role?
seoTitle: L-1 staff transfers: real duties and the new office
description: A senior title does not establish the person’s employment history or the work the U.S. business will support.
learningSummary: An L-1 plan needs both a qualifying company relationship and a qualifying person and role. Moving an experienced technician into a job called general manager does not settle either.

sections.heading: The work abroad and company connection
paragraphs: The regulation generally requires one continuous year of qualifying full-time employment abroad within the relevant preceding three years, alongside the prescribed organisational relationship. Record the actual employment and travel: brief lawful U.S. trips have specific treatment and are not automatically counted as foreign employment.
A licence or supplier relationship does not itself establish the qualifying corporate link. The separate company-relationship guide explains that distinction.

sections.heading: Who will do the customer work?
paragraphs: A qualifying manager’s work concerns managing an organisation or function, with the required authority and discretion. First-line supervision alone does not make someone a manager, subject to the professional-employee qualification. Executive and specialised-knowledge roles have their own elements.

In a fictional launch, a group proposes its technical leader as U.S. manager but supplies only a title and budget. The missing explanation is the real job: technical versus management duties, time allocation, reporting lines, supporting staff and authority. Someone must still perform the customer work while the claimed manager manages.

sections.heading: The new-office plan must support the claimed position
paragraphs: For a new-office manager/executive, the regulation requires sufficient physical premises and evidence that the operation will support the qualifying position within one year of approval, including the proposed organisation and financial ability. Specialised-knowledge new-office provisions differ.

An owner or major stockholder has additional specified temporary-service/assignment-abroad evidence under the cited provision. These are not a generic minimum-investment rule. Founder relocation need not be assumed if the independently assessed staffing plan allows the owner to remain abroad.

practicalOutput: Check the person’s actual foreign employment and U.S. duties against the relevant role before making the launch depend on the transfer.
limitations: No role or petition is approved here. Current forms, fees, processing times, blanket routes and admission require separate checks.
editNote: Cut the repeated evidence table and matrix instructions; retained the real-duty problem and the complete named new-office conditions.
conditionsRetained: Continuous qualifying full-time foreign year in relevant prior3years and trip treatment retained.
Qualifying organisation and role separate; no licence/title proof.
Manager authority/discretion; firstline/professional qualification; executive/specialknowledge distinct.

title: Does P.L. 86-272 protect your service income?
seoTitle: P.L. 86-272 limits for service businesses
description: A narrow goods-solicitation protection does not settle service income or every state tax.
learningSummary: P.L. 86-272 concerns specified solicitation of orders for physical goods and state or local net-income tax. A service business cannot simply borrow that protection because it sells across borders.

sections.heading: The protection has conditions
paragraphs: The person’s only in-state activities must be the specified solicitation of orders for tangible personal property. The orders must meet the out-of-state approval/rejection and fulfilment conditions. The statute also excludes specified state-incorporated corporations and resident or domiciled individuals.

Even for goods, this is not protection from sales/use, payroll, unemployment or gross-receipts taxes, or an answer to company qualification. Its defined independent-contractor treatment is not a general worker-status ruling.

sections.heading: No office does not mean no tax
paragraphs: A fictional foreign service brand contracts for work at U.S. customer sites but has no local office. Its assumption—no office, no tax—skips what it sells, who works where and which tax is involved.

Cleaning, consulting, training and managed IT services do not become physical-goods solicitation by analogy. But failure to establish this protection does not itself prove a particular state tax or return is due. That answer depends on the actual state, tax and activities.

practicalOutput: Identify the income and tax involved before relying on a goods-solicitation rule to price a service contract.
limitations: This explains the federal boundary only; it determines no state/local tax connection, threshold, sourcing, apportionment, taxability or return obligation.
editNote: Removed the duplicate activity table, self-check and register; retained the service-income misconception and statutory boundaries.
conditionsRetained: Only specified solicitation, tangiblegoods, netincometax and out-of-state approval/fulfilment conditions retained.

title: What does Texas’s data-processing exemption actually reduce?
seoTitle: Texas data processing: service classification and taxable value
description: The 20% provision reduces qualifying value; it is not a 20% tax rate.
learningSummary: Texas treatment follows what the customer receives, not whether you call the business IT or the invoice consulting.

sections.heading: Data work and professional judgement are different
paragraphs: The Comptroller describes entering, storing, manipulating or retrieving customer data as data processing. Merely using a computer to provide a professional service is different; the guidance contrasts data tasks with engineering or bookkeeping judgement and interpretation.
The statutory category has exclusions. A contract containing data entry, storage and advice needs its actual deliverables considered. Renaming the whole invoice consulting does not explain the work.

sections.heading: Fictional example: $1,000 becomes an $800 base
paragraphs: The named Texas sections include data processing among taxable services and exempt 20% of the value of information services and data processing services. If $1,000 is otherwise-taxable qualifying data-processing value, $200 is exempt and $800 remains before other applicable adjustments.
That does not calculate the tax itself. The actual rate and other facts still matter; nor does this arithmetic establish that your service belongs in the category.

sections.heading: Mixed services and use outside Texas need evidence
paragraphs: The Comptroller publication addresses distinct, identifiable nontaxable services, reasonable separate charges and supporting documentation for mixed bundles. It also addresses use inside and outside Texas. Describe the work, charges and customer use rather than changing only an invoice heading.
Service classification, taxable value, the seller’s tax connection or registration, sourcing and final rate are separate questions.

practicalOutput: Describe the actual invoice lines and customer use, then apply any supported value exemption separately from the tax rate.
limitations: Texas example only, using the named statutory sections and Comptroller guidance revision 03/2022. No actual allocation, exemption, permit, sourcing or collection obligation is determined.
editNote: Kept the useful value calculation once and removed the question-only mixed-contract table and tax-schedule instructions.

title: A UK receiving company does not itself establish treaty relief
seoTitle: UK royalty treaty benefits: why incorporation is not enough
description: Residence, entitlement to the income and the selected treaty-eligibility route are separate conditions.
learningSummary: Registering a UK company does not by itself support a reduced U.S. royalty-withholding assumption. Identify the actual recipient and the treaty conditions it can establish.

sections.heading: An address is not the entitlement test
paragraphs: IRS guidance identifies treaty residence, beneficial ownership, derivation of income and applicable limitation-on-benefits conditions. Beneficial ownership concerns entitlement to the income, not merely receiving a bank payment. The payer must consider actual knowledge or reason to know of ineligibility.

In a fictional group, finance proposes paying royalties to a new UK company. The registration certificate does not establish who owns it during the relevant period, how it derives the income or what deductible payments leave it. These can matter to the particular eligibility route.

sections.heading: Use the actual treaty route and amended text
paragraphs: Article 4 defines residence. Article 12 covers royalties with permanent-establishment, special-relationship and conduit conditions. Article 23 contains several limitation-on-benefits routes: the described Article 23(2)(f) ownership/base-erosion route has both ownership-period and deductible-payment conditions.

The July 2002 protocol replaces Article 23(7)(d). The unamended equivalent-beneficiary wording in the 2001 text is therefore not the complete provision. This review does not resolve derivative benefits, post-Brexit treatment or the recipient’s entitlement.

practicalOutput: Keep a proposed treaty reduction out of committed support cash until the actual recipient and claimed route are supported.
limitations: U.S.–UK illustration only; no rate, permanent-establishment, conduit or equivalent-beneficiary result is supplied. Other treaties and E-2 enterprise nationality are different inquiries.

title: Do trademark quality rules settle franchise classification?
seoTitle: Trademark quality rules versus operating controls
description: Protecting the quality of a branded service and directing the whole business are different legal questions.
learningSummary: A requirement can protect the brand and also affect how the operator runs the business. Its title does not decide its legal effect.

sections.heading: The trademark provisions concern marked goods and services
paragraphs: The cited trademark definition of a related company concerns the owner’s control over the nature and quality of the marked goods or services. The related-use provision addresses legitimate use and controlled first use benefiting the registrant or applicant, with its condition against public deception.
These provisions do not approve a particular staffing rule, software system or inspection programme. They also do not supply a complete opinion on licence validity or abandonment.

sections.heading: Logo approval and staff scheduling do different jobs
paragraphs: A fictional brand approves vehicle logos but also dictates job acceptance, staff allocation and customer scheduling through software. Explain both the quality outcome and the effect on the operating method. Neither logo approval nor software alone decides the complete relationship.

Federal franchise classification separately considers brand association, significant operating control or assistance and required payment. Removing every quality check is not the answer, nor does calling a broader rule trademark protection settle it. The linked control-and-assistance guide covers that wider question.

practicalOutput: Identify what each requirement actually controls before treating it as only trademark protection.
limitations: This is the statutory distinction, not a safe harbour or complete trademark case-law review. The May 2008 FTC guide is explanatory; current law and independent state franchise rules remain relevant.

title: A clean sanctions name search is not the whole answer
seoTitle: Sanctions screening: identity, ownership and the transaction
description: An unlisted business can still be affected through ownership, and different lists carry different restrictions.
learningSummary: A possible name match needs identity checking. A missing name does not settle ownership or whether the proposed deal is permitted.

sections.heading: Check the person and the source list
paragraphs: The Consolidated Screening List combines specified Commerce, State and Treasury lists as an aid. Commerce says apparent matches need further diligence and confirmation against the official source list. A fuzzy-name score measures similarity, not the chance a transaction is lawful.
Names, aliases, identifiers and addresses help match the actual party. Then identify the restriction associated with that particular list and person; not all list entries have the same effect.

sections.heading: Why multiplying the percentages can miss the result
paragraphs: OFAC’s 50 Percent Rule concerns relevant direct or indirect ownership of 50% or more in aggregate by blocked persons. In the cited illustration, a blocked person owns 50% of A, making A blocked; A owns 50% of B, which can in turn make B blocked. Looking only at 50% × 50% = 25% misses that intermediate-entity treatment.

Control without 50% aggregate ownership is not automatic blocking under this ownership rule. But other designation/blocking criteria or dealings involving a blocked representative can still matter. Below 50% is not universal permission.

sections.heading: The deal has separate restrictions
paragraphs: A distributor with no apparent name match still needs its relevant ownership and proposed goods, destination and use examined. Party screening alone does not settle technology, end-use, country-programme or authorisation requirements. A country connection is not necessarily a blanket ban either. Revisit the answer when the parties, ownership, goods or restrictions change.

practicalOutput: Resolve the actual identity, relevant ownership and transaction restrictions before relying on a clean-name result.
limitations: No live designation check, export classification, licence or transaction authorisation is provided here.

title: Who is proposing the common network price?
seoTitle: Franchise pricing: supplier policy versus competitor agreement
description: A request from competing operators is not simply another brand standard.
learningSummary: Before requiring a common price, identify who agrees, who competes and how the policy will be enforced. The federal standard for one type of supplier/dealer agreement does not approve every network arrangement.

sections.heading: When the operators ask for the price
paragraphs: In a fictional service network, independent operators ask the brand to set a common price. The brand also operates its own unit. Their competing relationships and communications matter: calling the resulting policy vertical does not remove possible coordination between competitors.

A supplier’s unilateral policy, a supplier/dealer agreement and competitor coordination are different situations. Distinguish suggested from required prices and identify discounts, advertising support or other methods used to induce compliance.

sections.heading: What Leegin changed—and what it did not decide
paragraphs: In Leegin v. PSKS (2007), the Supreme Court replaced the prior Dr. Miles federal per-se treatment of vertical minimum resale-price agreements with rule-of-reason analysis. That means examination of the actual arrangement and competitive context, not automatic approval. The Court reversed and remanded; this was not a ruling that every such policy or the particular arrangement was lawful.
The cited record establishes that standard and disposition, not an independently checked later merits result. State-law treatment can differ.

sections.heading: Do not treat different restrictions as one policy
paragraphs: Minimum advertised price (MAP), most-favoured-nation (MFN) terms linking treatment to other parties, territories and customer allocations need their actual terms examined. Federal, state and international rules may differ. A stated quality or service-investment purpose does not itself settle the competitive effects.

practicalOutput: Examine the actual price proposal and competing relationships before announcing a required network price.
limitations: No pricing, territory or customer restriction is cleared here, and no complete antitrust case-law survey is supplied.
editNote: Removed the repeated table and case quiz; placed the competing-operator request before the legal standard.
conditionsRetained: Unilateral/vertical/horizontal distinction; brand-operated unit and actualenforcement retained.

title: A contractor label does not decide the technician’s status
seoTitle: Worker classification: actual work and federal-source limits
description: Equipment ownership and a signed contractor clause are not a complete employment test.
learningSummary: Look at how the person actually earns money and works. Different wage, tax and state tests can apply. The Department of Labor’s opinion-letter numbering is now reconciled, but this review does not establish the latest appellate status or classify your worker.

sections.heading: Is the person operating an independent business?
paragraphs: Relevant facts include who sets prices and schedules, accepts jobs, hires helpers, makes entrepreneurial investments, markets to other customers and has a genuine opportunity for profit or loss. Include actual practice and reserved rights.

In a fictional maintenance arrangement, the brand sets mandatory schedules and prices while the technician buys equipment. The contract says independent contractor, but says little about outside customers, helpers or profit and loss. Neither the label nor that purchase answers the whole question. Specialised skill alone does not establish an independent business.

sections.heading: The tax and wage questions are separate
paragraphs: The codified 29 CFR Part 795 interpretation reviewed in November 2026 examines the whole activity through six nonexclusive factors. No one factor or selected subset necessarily controls; it is not a points tally or a replacement for governing court law.

IRS employment-tax guidance instead groups common-law evidence into behavioural control, financial control and the type of relationship. It also considers the whole relationship; a right to control can matter even for remote work. A tax result or relief provision does not decide federal wage-and-hour duties under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) or state unemployment and wage law.

sections.heading: An investigation policy is not a repeal
paragraphs: The Department of Labor’s May 2025 bulletin changes its investigation approach within its stated scope and discretion; it expressly does not change employee rights or employer responsibilities. The named 2019 opinion was withdrawn in 2021 and expressly reissued, with its text reproduced, as FLSA2025-2 on May 2, 2025. That opinion concerns supplied virtual-marketplace facts, not automatic contractor treatment for technicians. The February 2026 replacement proposal, including its proposed expansion to the Family and Medical Leave Act and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act, is not effective merely because comments closed.

The cited Colt & Joe Trucking order concerned standing and stated alternative failed or waived arguments; it did not classify every technician. These source types cannot be used interchangeably to declare contractor treatment available.

practicalOutput: Check the real control and independent-business facts before relying on contractor treatment in your staffing cost.
limitations: No worker, exemption, tax relief or state-law result is determined. The current governing test must be applied to the actual relationship.

title: Separate payroll does not always mean separate employer duties
seoTitle: Shared workers and different joint-employer tests
description: The same worker can raise responsibilities for more than one business under the applicable law.
learningSummary: If businesses share people or employment decisions, separate incorporation and payroll do not by themselves settle responsibility. The wage-law and labour-relations tests must be kept distinct.

sections.heading: A real agency example: hours at two businesses
paragraphs: The Department of Labor’s Opinion Letter FLSA2025-05 considered a restaurant and members club with represented shared operations, managers and workers. On those supplied facts, it concluded the worker’s hours had to be combined and both employers were responsible for compliance with the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), the federal wage-and-hour law.

The letter is limited to the facts supplied and is not a court judgment about every franchise. Its practical lesson is to examine shared hours and real operations, rather than stop at the two payroll names.

sections.heading: An outcome inspection is different from setting a worker’s shift
paragraphs: Identify who selects workers, sets pay and individual schedules, directs performance, disciplines and terminates. A check of the contracted service outcome and an instruction about a named worker’s shift should not both be labelled quality control. Mixed-purpose controls and actual practice matter; neither fact alone completes a legal test.
Franchise classification asks about brand, operating control or assistance and payments. It does not itself decide who has duties to workers.

sections.heading: Which federal law is being applied?
paragraphs: For federal labour-relations law, the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA), the reviewed February 2026 final action restores the 2020 text: the 2023 rule never took effect after court vacatur. Substantial direct and immediate control over one or more listed essential employment terms is central; indirect or unexercised reserved authority has the rule’s qualified supplementary role.

For federal wage-and-hour law (the FLSA), Part 791 is reserved, not a declaration that joint-employer liability disappeared. The Department of Labor’s April 2026 publication is a proposal, not an effective rule or franchise exemption. Governing court law and the actual employment facts remain relevant.

practicalOutput: Check shared-worker hours and actual employment decisions before treating two payrolls as two independent wage obligations.
limitations: This makes no joint-employer finding or full governing-court, bargaining-unit or state-law determination. The cited court record is not a complete current docket search.

title: An import certificate does not close a later safety complaint
seoTitle: Product certificates and later CPSC reporting duties
description: Certification and reporting serious new safety information are different responsibilities.
learningSummary: A certificate concerns the applicable product requirements. New information about a hazard can create a separate reporting question even when a certificate is already on file.

sections.heading: Identify the product and responsible certifier
paragraphs: The Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) scope and exclusions depend on the actual article, ordinary users, intended use and other agencies involved. A B2B invoice does not itself remove a product from that inquiry.

For covered imported finished products, Part 1110 defines the importer/certifier role, certificate contents and eFiling. Specified broker, owner, purchaser or consignee allocations are possible, but the identified certifier remains legally responsible for validity, accuracy, completeness and availability. The testing basis must match the actual applicable rules; a bought template is not proof. Keep the certificate and specified supporting records for at least five years from the certificate’s creation date, and meet the separate access and furnishing requirements.

sections.heading: An overheating report needs its own assessment
paragraphs: In a fictional example, a brand receives overheating information after assembling its import certificate file. The old certificate is not a reason to ignore the new facts.

Covered firms can have an immediate reporting duty when information reasonably supports the specified noncompliance, a potentially substantial product hazard or an unreasonable serious-injury/death risk. The rule interprets immediate as 24 hours, with its weekend/holiday computation. Do not wait for a complete risk estimate by default: a reasonable investigation is not automatic permission to delay once reportable information is known. A supplier’s promise to handle it does not settle every other party’s duty.

sections.heading: eFiling policy does not waive safety duties
paragraphs: The final action uses July 8, 2026 for most covered products and January 8, 2027 for specified foreign-trade-zone entries. The reviewed FAQ describes an initial policy against entry denial solely for missing eFiling data while certificate enforcement continues. That time-sensitive policy is not an exemption or guaranteed entry result.

practicalOutput: Bring new safety information promptly into the reporting assessment instead of treating the certificate as the end of the issue.
limitations: No product jurisdiction, technical test, reportable-defect, recall or shipment-clearance conclusion is made. The example does not decide whether its complaint is reportable.

title: Does overseas system access fall within the DOJ data programme?
seoTitle: DOJ data programme: covered access and scope limits
description: The rule concerns defined people, data and transactions, not every overseas login.
learningSummary: A U.S. server does not remove the question if a foreign user can read or edit the data. This page explains programme scope; detailed Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) technical requirements remain unverified, so it does not establish a compliant access arrangement.

sections.heading: Who receives access?
paragraphs: Identify the U.S. person providing access as well as the foreign recipient, data and agreement.

paragraphs: Data brokerage and specified human-omic transactions have prohibitions. Relevant vendor, employment and investment transactions can be restricted, subject to actual security and other conditions, including the required diligence programme and annual audit.

title: Is your U.S. licence also a franchise?
seoTitle: Franchise vs licensing: the U.S. federal test
description: A brand licence can also be a franchise when the complete operating arrangement meets the federal test.
learningSummary: Calling the contract a licence does not decide which rules apply. A brand, a way to run the business and required payments must be examined together.

sections.heading: What the federal rule examines
paragraphs: The Federal Trade Commission’s Franchise Rule examines a continuing commercial relationship with three elements: association with a trademark or other commercial symbol; significant control over, or assistance with, the operator’s method of doing business; and a required payment or commitment.

A licence grants permission to use specified rights. If you also supply the operating system, the arrangement may raise franchise duties. Calling the operator an investor, distributor or licensee does not change the actual rights, support and payments.

sections.heading: Why separate purchases can form one system
paragraphs: In a fictional maintenance offer, the operator receives branded vans, mandatory scheduling software, initial training and required inspection methods, and pays a licence fee. These features work together to shape how the service is run.

The important questions are what the training teaches, what the software controls, how much discretion the operator retains and which payments are unavoidable. Software alone does not decide the test. Three separate invoices for the licence, training and software do not remove the need to consider the complete arrangement.

sections.heading: An exemption is a separate question
paragraphs: Once the arrangement is described accurately, examine any federal exclusion or exemption and its conditions. An exemption from specified duties does not necessarily change the relationship’s definition. Include promises made in presentations and ordinary practice, not just the signed contract, and payments to related companies.
State definitions and sales requirements are independent. A federal conclusion does not settle the states connected with the seller, buyer, offer or proposed outlet.

practicalOutput: Before offering the arrangement, compare the contract, actual support promises and all required payments as one business model.
limitations: This is the federal starting point; it does not classify your arrangement or establish an exemption. State and local requirements remain separate.
editNote: Replaced repeated table, glossary, departmental checklist and factsheet instructions with one explanation and the original maintenance example.
conditionsRetained: Continuing commercial relationship and all three federal elements; control OR assistance must be significant.

title: When does your support shape the operator’s whole business?
seoTitle: Significant franchise control or assistance: what matters
description: The practical reach and importance of support matter more than the name or length of a manual.
learningSummary: A new operator may depend on your systems to price work, allocate staff and find customers. That helps explain the federal inquiry into significant operating control or assistance.

sections.heading: Look at the overall operating method
paragraphs: The question is not whether you provide any help. Consider its content, significance and the operator’s reasonable reliance on it in running the business. Contractual rights to impose controls matter as well as intervention already exercised. Include pre-contract promises and routine support.
The FTC’s May 2008 explanatory guide discusses training, accounting systems, management advice and detailed manuals. It is context to read with the current rule, not a current threshold sheet.

sections.heading: A short appendix can carry substantial operating rules
paragraphs: A fictional facilities brand has a logo guide covering colours and approved name use. Its quality appendix also determines accepted accounts, staffing, sales scripts, mandatory software, service reports and remedial visits.

The second document can shape the operating business even though it is called an appendix. A requirement solely protecting legal ownership of a mark differs from broader operating instructions. But neither a logo guide nor one software subscription decides the complete test, and counting features is not a substitute for assessing the relationship.

practicalOutput: Examine what your mandatory systems and promised help actually determine before treating them as incidental to a licence.
limitations: This explains one federal element, not complete franchise status or an exemption. Current law and independent state tests remain relevant.
editNote: Removed the duplicate appendix table and inventory; kept a short companion explaining reliance and practical reach.

title: Which payments count toward the $735 federal exemption?
seoTitle: The $735 franchise exemption: required payments and commitments
description: The relevant total is not just the first invoice, and exactly $735 does not pass a less-than test.
learningSummary: The exemption requires the relevant required payments or commitments to total less than $735. Count the whole arrangement, including covered affiliate payments and the specified period.

sections.heading: Use the amount, period and recipients together
paragraphs: Under the stated federal exemption, aggregate required payments or commitments to the franchisor or an affiliate from before operations begin through six months after they commence. The total must be less than $735; exactly $735 is not less. Older material quoting $500 does not give the current amount for this exemption.
Required means the rule’s actual definition, including contractual or practically necessary payments and its exclusions. A commitment can matter before cash is collected.

sections.heading: Fictional example: $300 is not the whole price
paragraphs: A brand requires a $300 initial fee, $250 training payment and $250 software commitment to its affiliate within the relevant period. Assuming all three are required payments under the rule, $300 + $250 + $250 = $800. The amount condition is not met on those assumptions.
Collecting the software money later does not establish that the obligation was undertaken later. Check the commitment as well as the payment date; an unknown required amount is not zero.

sections.heading: The inventory exclusion is specific
paragraphs: The payment definition excludes reasonable quantities of inventory bought at bona fide wholesale prices for resale or lease. It does not exclude every supply purchase. Equipment or materials consumed in providing a service are not automatically inventory for resale.
This is an exemption from specified federal disclosure duties, not the franchise definition or an exemption from state franchise, business-opportunity, dealer, advertising or relationship law.

practicalOutput: Count required commitments, their recipients and timing before relying on the low-payment exemption.
limitations: The page establishes no actual exemption or approved payment structure; the full definition and transaction facts still matter.
